Metadata.title: SecureCargo — Physics-tested cargo securement
Metadata.description: Check before the trip whether a truck's cargo is well distributed and properly secured: photo, physics simulation and a lashing plan that follows Brazilian rules.

hero.title: Physics-tested cargo securement.
hero.subtitle: Simulate the trip before the truck leaves: see what slides, what tips and what to fix.
hero.photoAlt: Black-and-white photograph of cargo held down by straps on a truck.

problem.label: Problem
problem.title: A load is checked with a look and a pull on the strap.
problem.p1: Before a trip, the driver walks around the truck, tugs each strap and decides it is good enough.
problem.p2: That check says nothing about a hard stop, a tight curve or a pothole.
problem.p3: Brazil has detailed rules for lashing cargo and for the weight each axle may carry. They are legal text. On the loading dock, what is needed is a yes or a no for this cargo, on this truck.
problem.photoAlt: Black-and-white photograph of a freight loading area.

solution.label: Our solution
solution.title: We run the trip before the truck leaves.
solution.body: SecureCargo builds the load from a photo and drives it through braking, curves and potholes in a physics simulation. It shows what moves, why, and the smallest change that fixes it.

photo.title: Photo
photo.body: Photograph the loaded truck bed. AI marks the cargo and the straps; you confirm or correct them.

simulation.body: A physics engine drives the load through hard braking, curves and potholes, and records what slides or tips.

emergency-braking.as_loaded: As loaded, the pallets slide forward and one hits the headboard.
emergency-braking.fixed: With two straps per pallet, the load does not move.

weigh-station.as_loaded: The load holds, but the rear axle is over the legal limit.
weigh-station.fixed: With the machine moved forward, both axles are within the limit.

rope-lashing.as_loaded: Tied with rope, the stacks slide sideways in the lane change.
rope-lashing.fixed: On anti-slip mats and under straps, the stacks do not move.

sharp-curve.as_loaded: Standing free, the cabinets tip over and fall off the truck.
sharp-curve.fixed: With two straps each, the cabinets stay upright.

steel-coil.as_loaded: As loaded, the coil rolls forward into the headboard.
steel-coil.fixed: In a cradle of two chocks, the coil does not move.

box-truck.as_loaded: The loose cartons slide the length of the box and slam into the front wall.
box-truck.fixed: Stacked against the front wall with a load bar behind, the cartons stay put.

dirt-road.as_loaded: The vibration loosens the straps, and the pallets slide when the truck brakes.
dirt-road.fixed: With diagonal straps at the corners, the pallets do not move.

anti-slip-mat.as_loaded: On the bare floor, the plastic pallets slide forward under braking.
anti-slip-mat.fixed: On anti-slip mats, the same two straps hold them.

full-trip.as_loaded: Unlashed, the crates creep forward on the descent and slide on at the final stop.
full-trip.fixed: With three straps per crate, nothing moves for the whole trip.

emergency-braking.as_loaded: Three pallets with one strap each. One strap does not press a pallet down hard enough for friction to hold it in an emergency stop.
emergency-braking.fixed: The same pallets with two straps each, the number the EN 12195-1 standard asks for with its safety factor. Friction holds with room to spare.

weigh-station.as_loaded: An 8 t machine chained down near the back of the bed. Nothing moves over the speed bump, but most of its weight lands on the rear axle and the steering axle is left light.
weigh-station.fixed: The same machine moved forward, over the middle of the wheelbase. Its weight is shared between the two axles.

rope-lashing.as_loaded: Stacks on plastic pallets, each tied with two ropes. Rope stretches and cannot be tightened like a ratchet strap, and Brazilian rules do not allow it as cargo lashing.
rope-lashing.fixed: Rubber anti-slip mats under the pallets and two ratchet straps per stack.

sharp-curve.as_loaded: Two tall cabinets with no lashing. The curve pushes them sideways harder than their narrow base can resist.
sharp-curve.fixed: Two straps over each cabinet press it down and keep it from tipping.

steel-coil.as_loaded: A 10 t coil lying across the bed, "eye to the side", with nothing in front of it. A cylinder needs no friction to move: braking makes it roll.
steel-coil.fixed: The same coil in a cradle: a 20 cm chock on each side. It would take 0.88 g of braking to roll it over a chock; the truck can brake at 0.64 g on a wet road.

box-truck.as_loaded: Six cartons left at the back of the box with nothing around them. Cardboard on plywood has a friction factor of only 0.3, and in fog the driver brakes late and hard.
box-truck.fixed: The same cartons stacked in two layers against the front wall, with a load bar behind them. The wall takes what friction cannot, well within its rating.

dirt-road.as_loaded: Pallets of sacks under three straps each. That is enough on this dusty deck while the straps are tight, but hours of vibration halve their tension before the final stop.
dirt-road.fixed: Four diagonal straps from the corners of each pallet to the bed. They hold by their strength, not by their tension, so loosening does not matter.

anti-slip-mat.as_loaded: Three stacks on plastic pallets, two straps each, on the plywood floor. Plastic on plywood has a friction factor of 0.2, so the straps would have to press very hard.
anti-slip-mat.fixed: The same pallets and straps, on rubber anti-slip mats with a friction factor of 0.6.

full-trip.as_loaded: Six 1.5 t crates on a semi-trailer, left without lashings because they are heavy. Weight does not help: friction grows with it, and so does inertia.
full-trip.fixed: Three straps over each crate, the number EN 12195-1 asks for. They hold through the descent, the speed bump and the emergency stop.
